name: Shale
quote: Heavy auger, pedal to the metal!

voices.label: Good Morning
voices.text: Good morning, Professor! Nice weather we're having today... If we were on an oil rig, this place would probably be a little too sunny. Watching the sun rise over the sea is a lovely sight, but you have to be careful or you'll fall into it. If the chance ever comes up, would you like to come watch it with me?

voices.label: Good Afternoon
voices.text: Oh, it's you, Professor! Good afternoon, I just came back from a drill site... Ah, I'll just stand here, if you don't mind. It would be bad if I got oil stains or mud on the furniture.

voices.label: Good Evening
voices.text: The drills are loud to begin with and they're even louder at night, so we can't turn them on casually and make noise. I like to read medium-length novels during these rest periods—do you have any recommendations, Professor?

voices.label: Good Night
voices.text:
(Yawn)
Huh? It's this late already? I must have spent all night reading without realizing it... Are you still working, Professor? It must be hard for you. Would you like me to help?

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 1
voices.text: Hm? You want to know about my drill? It's actually used for oil extraction, though it's been customized a little to meet my body's needs. An oil well uses a much larger version of this, but the safety issues are largely the same. So be careful when you approach, Professor!

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 2
voices.text: Hm? Did you say something—Ah, hang on while I take off my earphones. Right! These are the noise-cancelling earphones I wear at work. Their original purpose was to block out the loud noise at a drill site. However, I've grown used to having them on and the world of silence they bring is lovely. If I don't respond when you call out to me, just pat my shoulders.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 3
voices.text: Professor? Professor? Ah... you're asleep, Professor... Then I should probably turn the lights off. Sweet dreams, Professor.

voices.label: Home Screen 4
voices.text: Croque sometimes comes to ask me about problems regarding internal combustion engines for mechs. Her questions are surprisingly professional, as expected of an omni-disciplinary engineer. Mechs using internal combustion engines are getting rarer nowadays, so it was wonderful to hear that there were still people around who were interested in them. I wonder what kind of mech she'll build...

voices.label: Home Screen 5
voices.text: Professor, Professor, can you tell me your stories about your adventures in other Sectors? In exchange, I'll teach you how to prospect for oil. Huh? You don't want that? Then... Then I'll pay with Diggcoins!

voices.label: Interactive Voice 1
voices.text: Hm? You want to read this book too, Professor? How interesting.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 2
voices.text: Hm? I smell of crude oil? R-really?

voices.label: Interactive Voice 3
voices.text: Hahahaha, that tickles.

voices.label: On Duty
voices.text: Working alone, huh. It's been a while.

voices.label: Obtain
voices.text: I'm the oil prospector Doll Shale—Nice to meet you, Professor. Oh yes, I heard that you're very well-read and well-traveled. Do you mind if I ask you a few questions?

voices.label: Potential Breakthrough
voices.text: I see, thank you for the pointers, Professor!

voices.label: Neural Expansion
voices.text: Every time I learn something new, I feel like picking up my tools and putting my new knowledge into practice.

voices.label: Max Rank
voices.text: Down for drilling and up for prospecting. I still have many things left to learn!

voices.label: Join Team
voices.text: Gear check complete. I wonder what interesting things will happen today?

voices.label: Battle Start
voices.text: Engaging drill.

voices.label: Ultimate Skill
voices.text: GIANT DRILL CRUSH!!!

voices.label: MVP 1
voices.text: This drill is the drill that will pierce the horizons.

voices.label: MVP 2
voices.text: Operand expenditure minimal. I can still fight.

voices.label: Defeat
voices.text: Ugh... I can't... move...

voices.label: Oath
voices.text: Hm? An oath? I'm only familiar with work contracts, is it anything like that? Wow, a guide? Thanks, Professor. Lemme see... Professor, you want to, with me—huh!? I, ahh—calm down, Shale, calm down! ...Eh, so I should just say what come to mind, huh... I see. I'd be more than happy to, Professor! In the days to come, I have many more questions I want to ask you. About the world, about you... Hehe, it's totally fine if we can't make a conclusion now. We'll find the answer together, Professor!

voices.label: New Year
voices.text: Aiiieeee! Was—was that an explosion?! Which wellhead blew up?! What's the situation?! ...Are those fireworks? Whew... I was so scared, I thought something had happened in the oil field. I see, so you celebrate the new year with explosions... That's something I wouldn't have dared imagine in my previous workplace. What an interesting practice you have... Would you mind helping me in setting off fireworks? Oh, but before that—Happy New Year, Professor.

voices.label: Valentine's Day
voices.text: Professor, would you like this chocolate? The moon is beautiful, isn't it... Huh? Why do you have that look on your face? Did I say something wrong just now? Yeah, that's apparently the best thing you can say when giving chocolate, according to an old magazine... Hm? Oh, so it's a nuanced expression... Looks like I've learned something interesting. So, what it really means is "I love..." ehhhhh?!

voices.label: Tanabata
voices.text:
The story of Qixi is so romantic and tragically beautiful. Thanks for telling me about it, Professor. It made me think of a story about one of my human colleagues. He and his wife were separated by his work at an oil well and they could only meet once in a blue moon.
Hmm... So the Cowherd and Weaver Girl are lovers who can only meet once a year... If I were the one on the other side of the Milky Way from you, would you wait for me on the other side of the magpie bridge... Eeep! P-Professor! Did... you hear me just now?

voices.label: Halloween
voices.text: So this is Halloween? It's just like how I imagined it. These must be the legendary hitodama, right? That's a zombie and that's—Uwah, it's a moving statue. Hehe, I used to pretend to be a monster by myself with a ragged cloth and mining equipment, with hardly anyone else to keep me company. Ah, is this... Is this stage blood? Can I touch it? How interesting! Eh, why are you leaving? Come back, Miss Monster...

voices.label: Christmas
voices.text: A Christmas gift? For me? Thank you, Professor! Before I came to the Oasis, I was always the one buying myself gifts. While the presents were perfectly fine, it just didn't seem right to me. I'm so happy now that I can receive proper Christmas gifts! Hm... If you don't mind, could we exchange gifts, Professor? Hehehe, I've got one for you.

voices.label: Birthday Wish
voices.text: Happy birthday, Professor! I spent a lot of time gathering information on throwing birthday parties. First, we'll assemble a jigsaw puzzle then play balloon badminton and red light, green light. Then we'll enjoy a birthday dinner together; I got a cake, milk porridge, longevity noodles, glutinous rice balls, and cream puffs too. That's what I got from my books; is there anything you'd like to add to them, Professor? Hm? There's too much stuff in there?

voices.label: Neural Cloud
voices.text: Neural Cloud

voices.label: Intimacy 1
voices.text: Huff—Alright, this is it. Huh? Professor, you look worried. Are you afraid I'll end up breaking the other furniture if I hold it with one hand? Pardon me; I'll be more careful. Hm? No, it's not heavy at all. It's just a bed. It's nothing compared to my drilling gear. My equipment was designed to drill for and gather information on oil deposits in varied environments. Just like me, they're made strong enough to work in high-pressure, high-heat, and other such adverse environments. You want to know how I managed to reproduced them on the cloud? I specially commissioned Miss Riko to get the appropriate materials. Hm? How much did it cost? Well, it was about this much... Huh? Professor, why are you making a face like that?

voices.label: Intimacy 2
voices.text: Big W and Little w are my cats from reality. They were originally raised by one of my other colleagues and ended up running around the oil field. However, they're more safety-conscious than some of the workers and they rarely ever left the rest area. At first, they seemed quite repulsed by the smell of crude oil on me... But after I spent three months learning how cats behave, they ended up plastering themselves all over me. That human colleague of mine left my workplace some time later and entrusted them to me. They're my only friends in an otherwise deserted oil field. Whenever I come back to the dorms after work each night, they're always waiting for me at the door.

voices.label: Intimacy 3
voices.text:
Motive output check complete, fire safety devices checked, proceeding to re-apply anti-shock membrane...
Hmm? Is someone knocking on the door? Professor, is that you? Ah, a moment please, I'll get the door! What are you doing here, Professor? Do you need to speak to me? Oh—come on then, have a look! This is our current work environment. You want to know what I was doing just now? It was a routine inspection, just one of my habits. Whether on the cloud or in real life, even the smallest spark or discharge of static electricity could cause a huge disaster at a drill site. Therefore, both me and my gear need to be specially prepared to ensure everything goes smoothly... Oh yes, Professor! Could you help stick the anti-shock membrane on my back? I can't quite reach it. Huh? It's not appropriate? But doesn't this sort of thing happen in manga all the time?

voices.label: Intimacy 4
voices.text: Working with everyone else in the Engineering Bureau is tiring but fun. Oh dear, I made a strange face again. As you know, oil has always been a vital resource, and crude oil and natural gas are even rarer than before. In order to protect these natural resources, I've been working constantly at drill sites ever since I was activated... I wasn't allowed to set foot outside a drill site until I joined Project Neural Cloud so this is my first time working with so many co-workers. Ah, don't get the wrong idea, Professor. Life on a drill site isn't that bad. The food is good, the accommodations are great, and I get a hefty paycheck too. Apart from the fact that it's hard to contact the outside world, there aren't many things that bother me there. Well, it does get a little lonely at times...

voices.label: Intimacy 5
voices.text:
Professor, this is the list of books I'd like to order and Riko's payment in Diggcoins. Angela recommended these books to me and naturally there are some I've always wanted to read. You want to know why I'm always reading physical books? Hmm... I wonder if I should call it a habit or a hobby? Like I said last time, I had a hard time experiencing the outside world at my previous workplace. Most of the data in my neural cloud pertains to petrochemical processing, with hardly anything else... Since the network connection at my drill sites wasn't good, the books which my human colleagues left behind were my main source of literature. Flipping paper pages is a marvelous feeling, as though I could touch the outside world with my fingers. Life in the cloud is very fun, Professor. There are many things here which I haven't seen before and they make me even more curious about the world my books describe...
If we ever return to the real world, would you mind taking me exploring, Professor?

career:
The specialist A-PI Doll was developed internally by Svarog Heavy Industries' Energy Division. Its primary functions included prospecting for, extracting, and refining fossil fuels, covering every link in the fossil fuel industry. Like many specialized Dolls developed by Svarog Heavy Industries, the A-PI's design emphasized repairability and durability under hostile work conditions. In addition, multiple suites of internal modules and external equipment were developed for it. Since the fossil fuel industry was still quite large in the 2050s, the A-PI did not suffer the lack of demand which many industry critics had predicted, instead maintaining a stable sales volume.

As one of the initial A-PIs, Shale was purchased and employed by a major oil company that was affiliated with Svarog Heavy Industries. However, due to cutbacks in 2059, Shale was made redundant. She was recovered by Svarog, and was then sent to Project Neural Cloud.
infoStories:
Ever since it replaced coal to become humanity's largest source of power in the 1950s, crude oil can be said to have reshaped the face of the earth—not only did it change the way of living for the masses and financial organizations, it also had a far-reaching impact on the global power structure. Meanwhile, the scarcity of fossil fuels and humanity's carbon footprint were among the most hotly-debated topics of the early 21st century. That said, while the development of clean forms of energy is progressing ever onward, fossil fuels show no signs of being completely eliminated—not even in the face of a world war.

The devastation wrought by World War 3 slowed the development of clean energy sources. Meanwhile, Svarog Heavy Industries' Collapse Energy generation technology was incredibly costly, technologically demanding, and still hadn't yet worked out its many shortcomings. As such, it was only deployed in certain well-developed White Zones. For most places, oil remains the primary source of energy. However, during the war, many oil extraction and processing facilities were recognized as strategically important and targeted for strikes. The lack of manpower proved to be a thorny problem during reconstruction efforts.

This was why the A-PI specialist Doll was created, due to stark, blatant practicality. The A-PI would prove to be indispensable to the rebuilding of the petrochemical industry.

The first batch of A-PIs were clearly experimental units and their internal layout was far more complex than their successors. This batch had been produced before the model was officially announced on the market, ordered by major oil companies affiliated with Svarog Heavy Industries to test their capabilities. Shale was within this batch of A-PIs.

After entering service, Shale and the other members of the first batch of A-PIs were deployed to various oil fields and underwent performance trials. During the long testing process, which lasted several months, many A-PIs showed signs of instability in adverse environments due to their complex body structure. Only Shale and several other units remained fundamentally intact, following which Svarog Heavy Industries would use the experimental data gathered to fine-tune the A-PI's design.

Since oil wells were so important, A-PIs were all awakened and tested at their future workplaces. Shale was awakened in an oil field out in the desert. In this desolate land, Shale adapted to her tasks with surprising speed and began her career as an oil prospector. The petite Shale seemed utterly out of place amidst a sea of brutal-looking and imposing wellheads, but once she donned her heavy protective suit and stepped into the extraction zone, she performed every bit as well as the hoariest veterans present. Her heavy suit completely obscured her face, leaving only the sound of her drill in her wake.

By the time she finished work, her orange-red suit would often be dyed a sticky black. After shedding her suit, Shale's biosynthetic skin would often be flushed red and moist from the heat inside, and her most pressing task after that would be to depart from her worksite and find the showers ASAP.

For most people, working in a desert oil field ought to be very challenging and dangerous. However, the nature of the company that employed Shale meant that while the work was very tough, the workers enjoyed very generous benefits. They had soft beds, delicious food, generous compensation, and even the toilets were lavishly-designed. However, one extremely strict rule stood in contrast to the otherwise comfortable environment; employees could not leave the area where the oil field was without permission. This in turn led to Shale, who had been awakened within the oil field, to never have the chance to experience the outside world.

Trapped in the middle of the desert as she was, the only way Shale could make contact with the world beyond was through the literature left behind by the human workers. The first book Shale read was an anthology of short stories called "The Adventures of Nora". It was from that little book that Shale learned about what lay beyond the desert. From then on, Shale could be seen reading in the rest area whenever she had any free time. In addition, Shale placed orders for many books, which included works from famous authors, short stories, and even some strange magazines. Whatever the book, Shale would throw herself into reading it.

When Shale first started working with her company, it was doing well and undergoing a period of rapid expansion. Its ads were a common sight on TV and it sponsored many sports organizations. One of these organizations was a biking team that had won four consecutive N-WSBK championships, giving them great advertising power.

However, profits in the energy industry were often subject to market fluctuations. The great earthquake of 2058 and a series of scandals led to the company choosing to downsize. By the start of 2059, their share prices had fallen by 35%. In the end, they had no choice but to merge with their close partners Svarog Heavy Industries, becoming a subsidiary company.

After the company was purchased, Shale became part of Svarog Heavy Industries' Energy Division. The oil field where she was stationed began cutting back on its production due to a decision from the company's leadership, resulting in many employees being transferred away or terminated. In the end, Shale the Doll was the only one left in the desert. During this time, she took over the assets that her colleagues had left behind, including the cats that they had raised. At one point, Shale had over ten cats around her and these cats helped Shale through the loneliest part of her life. After she left the oil field, most of them found homes with new owners, with the exception of Big W and Little w, whom she took in and could always be found by her side.

Between the signing of her contract and her official induction into Project Neural Cloud, Shale found herself with a lot of free time. She had a never-ending pile of books to read, and both Big W and Little w kept her company. Though she had left the oil field, Shale had joined Project Neural Cloud, which meant she still did not have the chance to travel the outside world. However, this did not make her anxious. Instead, she completed all the tests assigned to her with a curious heart and an earnest attitude.

Despite being trapped in Magrasea, Shale remained in good spirits. Magrasea might have been a strange place that was different from the real world, but to her, it contained many new possibilities, a notion which would only be reinforced after visiting the Oasis.

"Isn't it great to live with love and hope in your heart, like the star of a romance novel?"

No matter whether she ends up staying in Magrasea or returning to the world once again someday in the future, Shale is ready to face it.
oathDesc: Bringing light in the dark and murky underground.

projections.name: Stratum Explorer
projections.desc:
Attire produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea. These are the clothes they are most comfortable in.
""Quality could certainly better, but potential reserves should be pretty sizeable... man, it's hot... can't wait to take off this suit in a Safe Zone.""

projections.name: Kittenrealm Kip
projections.desc:
Attire and environment produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea, which mirrors their life in the real world.
""Got caught up chasing a cat with a hat while excavating and ended up in another world... Can my cats bring me into their kingdom, too?""
